claims: Newton cooling assumes dT/dt = −k(T−Ta). For constant surroundings Ta and factor k, the temperature gap is (T0−Ta)e^(−kt). Using one halving time as the time unit gives T = 20 + 60 × 2^(−t).
The cup identifies tea; color and liquid level do not encode temperature. Evaporation and changing surroundings can violate the simple model.
limitations: Numerical checks complement the stated derivation; idealizations are explicit.
